messages:
raj: Hi folks, new hire question — running kubectl from WSL2 (Ubuntu) on Windows. I merged the kubeconfig from the onboarding portal but `kubectl config get-contexts` shows two clusters and `kubectl get ns` errors with `error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)`. Any tips?

anya: Hey raj, welcome! Two quick things: 1) do you have an SSO/OIDC credential helper we use (gcp, okta, azure)? 2) check that your KUBECONFIG didn't silently concatenate with Windows line endings. Try `sed -n '1,120p' ~/.kube/config | sed -n '1,120p'` and `file ~/.kube/config`.

raj: Thanks. It's Okta SSO and I used the Windows file from Downloads then `cat > ~/.kube/config` to paste. `file` reports "with CRLF line terminators".

kevin: Ah yeah CRLF will break base64 cert decoding sometimes. Run `dos2unix ~/.kube/config` in WSL or re-download the Linux tarball from the portal. Also confirm your okta-cred plugin is installed in WSL: `which okta-cred-helper` or `kubelogin --version`.

raj: dos2unix fixed the CRLF issue. Now `kubectl get ns` gives `error: exec plugin: invalid token: token expired`. How do I refresh SSO?

anya: For Okta we use `kubelogin` + `kubectl oidc-login`. Run `kubelogin --login`, follow the browser flow on Windows, then rerun `kubectl get ns`. If that hangs, check that the helper binary is in PATH inside WSL (we symlink it to `~/.local/bin`).

infra-bot: Reminder: SSO tokens expire after 1h. Use `kubelogin --token` to request a fresh token or `kubectl config set-credentials raj --exec-command=kubelogin` per docs: https://intranet.redwood.ai/devex/kube-sso

raj: `kubelogin --login` opened a browser and I completed auth. `kubectl get ns` returns namespaces now. One more thing: I tried `kubectl get pods -n platform` and got `Forbidden`. What's the process to request namespace access?

kevin: We do RBAC via the Access repo. Create a GitHub PR against infra/access-requests with a small YAML for the RoleBinding or use the access portal (link in onboarding). In the PR description include: your username, requested role (view/edit), namespaces, and justification. Tag @kevin or @anya for fast-track.

raj: Filed the PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123 — requested `view` for `platform` and `dev`.

access-bot: New access request created: infra PR #4123, requested by raj. Reviewer: kevin.

kevin: Approved and applied. You should see a change within 30s.

infra-bot: RBAC rolebinding applied by kevin at 1772000062.

raj: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n platform` now returns "yes". All set, thanks everyone! :wave:`
